source.title: Electrically active hydrogels based on PEDOT:PSS for neural cultures

material: Alg–Lam-PEDOT:PSS 0.6 (0.6 wt% PEDOT:PSS, used for cell culture)

formulation.evidence: All cell culture data presented in this study were obtained with an electrically active hydrogel with 0.6 wt% concentration of PEDOT:PSS loaded in the hydrogel matrix.

description.evidence: the electrically active hydrogels preserved their shape and size over four weeks when immersed in cell media and exposed in a cell incubator (Fig. S8)

duration_days.evidence: the electrically active hydrogels preserved their shape and size over four weeks when immersed in cell media and exposed in a cell incubator (Fig. S8)

stability.conditions: immersed in cell media in incubator

biology.coating: poly-D-lysine + laminin (well plate; hydrogel in parallel)

culture_days.evidence: the neuron differentiation and maturation timeline which spans over 28 days as shown in Fig. 5

viability_percent.evidence: We calculated 86.43%, 94.98% and 94.74% cortical neuron viability when cultured under controlled conditions, alongside the Alg–Lam hydrogel and the Alg–Lam-PEDOT:PSS hydrogel, respectively.

survival.evidence: We calculated 86.43%, 94.98% and 94.74% cortical neuron viability when cultured under controlled conditions, alongside the Alg–Lam hydrogel and the Alg–Lam-PEDOT:PSS hydrogel, respectively.
Live/dead assays revealed that the cell viability was over 90% in all cases (Fig. S9), proving the non-cytotoxic nature of the hydrogels.

notes: Cells grown on well plates alongside hydrogel samples (5 mm diameter, 1 mm thick). Stability tested for 0.3–1.2 wt% PEDOT:PSS with identical results.
